provenance.notes: Clean family batch, book archetype. Independent trucks under franchise ads, small tickets, so products stay cheap and lean on photo quotes, load pricing and realtor and estate routes. No franchise or marketplace names. Fresh Fern fails CTA contrast. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: What fits in a junk load
pageStructurePlus.contains: A visual guide to a single item, a quarter, half and full truckload, with everyday examples like a sofa, a garage corner or a basement, plus heavy-item surcharges
pageStructurePlus.why: Nobody knows what a 'half load' is. A picture of what fits lets people price their own junk before they call.

pageStructurePlus.section: What we haul and what we can't
pageStructurePlus.contains: Furniture, appliances, mattresses, yard waste, construction debris, hot tubs and sheds, and the list of paint, chemicals and other items they can't take, with local drop-off alternatives
pageStructurePlus.why: The first question is always 'will you take this'. Answering it on the page stops the calls that end in no.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How loads are sorted for donation, recycling and disposal, donation receipts where available, and the kinds of local charities and recyclers they use
pageStructurePlus.why: People feel guilty throwing out a good couch. Showing the donation and recycling path makes the haul easier to book.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Room-by-room estate cleanouts, keepsake and paperwork set-aside, working with families who live far away, realtor deadlines, and broom-clean finish
pageStructurePlus.why: Estate cleanouts are the biggest junk tickets and the most emotional. Families choose whoever explains how carefully the house will be handled.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Drywall, flooring, cabinets and demolition debris hauled same day, compared with renting a dumpster that sits in the driveway, and contractor account options
pageStructurePlus.why: Remodelers and DIY owners weigh hauling against a dumpster. Showing the trade-off wins the jobs that would have gone to a rental.

designDirections.name: Point, Price, Gone
designDirections.bestFor: One-truck haulers who need a load price, a photo quote and a call button on the first screen
designDirections.headlineSample: Junk removal in {City}, priced by the load, gone today
designDirections.whyItFits: Ultramarine Poster's loud blue and geometric display type feel quick and confident, like a truck that shows up on time.

designDirections.name: Book a Pickup Window
designDirections.bestFor: Two- or three-truck junk removal companies filling arrival windows online every day
designDirections.headlineSample: Book a junk pickup in {City}, arrival window and price upfront
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Fresh Fern, fails CTA contrast. Peach Sorbet keeps the same soft rounded type with a warm coral Book button that passes and feels approachable.

designDirections.name: Careful Cleanouts
designDirections.bestFor: Established haulers selling estate and full-house cleanouts to families, realtors and attorneys
designDirections.headlineSample: Estate cleanouts in {City}, handled with care and a firm date
designDirections.whyItFits: Private Vault's old-style serif and quiet gold accent feel discreet, which suits families sorting a parent's house.

openers.line: Your listing has great junk removal reviews and no Website button, so someone staring at an old sofa on the curb can't see a load price or book a pickup.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where that junk pickup search could land: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens Facebook, where the price for a half load of junk is somewhere in the comments. People want the number before they message.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link. Note where it lands and whether any price is visible without scrolling.
openers.linkLine: Your junk removal prices on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing is a free page with a quote form that doesn't send. Every one of those forms was somebody's garage of junk going to the next hauler.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one broken thing: a dead form, an old number, a builder banner. Note it.
openers.linkLine: A junk removal page with a quote form that works: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your hauling site wouldn't scroll past the banner on my phone. People book junk removal standing in the garage with the phone in one hand.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Junk removal, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing online says what a single item, a half load or a full truck of junk costs, so the shopper picks the franchise ad that shows a price, even when you're cheaper.
openers.hook: Check the listing, posts and any site for a load or item price. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Junk prices by the load, with pictures of what fits: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your before-and-after garage and basement cleanout posts are the best advert junk removal has, and they're gone from the feed in a few days.
openers.hook: Find one before-and-after cleanout post and note the room. Name it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: A cleanout gallery that stays put: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention you donated the good furniture instead of dumping it. That's what people feel guilty about, and it should sit right next to the junk removal price.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about donating, recycling or being careful. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where the junk goes, on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Spring garage cleanouts and end-of-month move-outs bring a wave of junk calls. A booking page with arrival windows catches the people who won't wait for a callback.
openers.hook: Use from March to June, or at the end of any month. Check for a post about being busy.
openers.linkLine: Spring junk pickups with arrival windows: {demo-link}

openers.line: You've posted a couple of full-house estate cleanouts. Families handling a parent's house want to read how it's done before they call anyone, and right now there's nothing to read.
openers.hook: Only if they've posted an estate or full-house job. Note the town if shown.
openers.linkLine: An estate cleanout page families can trust: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a junk removal helper. Good applicants check whether the outfit looks steady before they spend a summer hauling furniture for you.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a sign on the truck. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A hauling company page with a hiring section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your junk reviews come from {Neighborhood} and towns around it, but nothing online says how far the truck goes or whether there's a trip charge for the far side.
openers.hook: Find the furthest town in their reviews or posts and use it.
openers.linkLine: A coverage page for your junk removal truck: {demo-link}

openers.line: When someone finally decides the junk goes, they want it gone today. If you take same-day jobs, a page showing today's open windows beats every voicemail.
openers.hook: Look for 'same day' in their posts or listing. Call at 6pm and see if it goes to voicemail.

openers.line: Carrying a fridge down someone's stairs is where walls and floors get dinged. If your hauling crew is insured, that belongs on the page next to the price.
openers.hook: Look for 'insured' on their listing, truck or posts. Never claim what you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and care promises on one junk page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like a lot of your junk removal comes from realtors and landlords who know you. That works until their client searches you and finds a phone number and nothing else.
openers.hook: Look for reviews or posts that mention a realtor, landlord or property manager. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred cleanout customer should land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your post about {specific recent job} shows a full truck and an empty room. Hauls like that should sit beside a pickup button, not scroll away.
openers.hook: Pick their newest hauling post and name it: the shed, the hot tub, the basement, the estate.
openers.linkLine: That junk removal job on a page that books: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is a serious haul.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the Facebook page, but no price by the load and no way to book a pickup window. I put together a sample site with both, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last message got buried. Here's the sample junk removal site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It shows prices by the load with pictures of what fits, what you take and can't, where the junk goes, and a booking page with arrival windows. If it's not useful, tell me and I'll leave you alone.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for junk removal companies here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No worries, you're probably mid-haul. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} that shows prices by the load and books pickup windows, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a hauling business your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}, a couple of full truckloads."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, maybe after the last dump run?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: I get plenty of calls already.
objections.handler: "Then the site saves you time. A lot of those calls are 'do you take a piano' and 'what's a half load'. The page answers them, and you get booked jobs with a photo instead."

objections.objection: I can't price junk without seeing it.
objections.handler: "You don't have to promise a final price. Show the load sizes with a starting price, take a photo for anything odd, and confirm on site. That's how the franchise ads do it."

objections.objection: The franchises outspend me on ads.
objections.handler: "You don't need to outspend them. When someone compares, the local junk hauler with clear prices and real reviews looks like the better deal. The site is how they compare."

objections.objection: I'm on a lead app already.
objections.handler: "Those leads go to several haulers at once and you pay either way. People who find your own junk removal site only get you."

objections.objection: My buddy said he'd make me a site.
objections.handler: "Totally fair. If he does, make sure it has load prices, a photo quote and pickup windows. If it stalls, this one's already built."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's load pricing, the photo quote, the estate cleanout page and booking. A couple of full junk loads covers it."

email.subject: Junk removal site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for junk removal companies in {City}, and I made a sample site for {Business Name} with load prices and online booking. I'll text you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} junk removal demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — end-of-year move-outs and holiday garage cleanouts in {City} are close, and people book whoever shows a load price first. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a couple of full truckloads, never to a single-item pickup.
Load pricing with pictures of what fits is the core. Price the photo quote and the estate page around it.
Price the estate cleanout page higher; it serves the biggest tickets and needs the most careful copy.
Charge separately for contractor debris pages; remodelers are a different buyer with repeat work.
Keep monthly items well below one single-item pickup, so they never feel like a lost job.
Never write a disposal or recycling claim the owner can't back up; price the 'where it goes' page from their real partners.

lineItems.description: Max with single-item, quarter, half and full load pricing, heavy-item surcharges and a visual for each size.
Max when it takes several photos, asks about stairs and access, and texts the owner a ready-to-answer request.
Max with a keepsake set-aside process, out-of-town family coordination, realtor deadlines and a walkthrough request.

lineItems.item: Renovation debris page with contractor accounts
lineItems.description: Max with a dumpster comparison, recurring pickup requests for contractors and monthly invoicing options.
Max when it names the kinds of local partners the owner really uses and explains donation receipts.

lineItems.item: Town pages for the truck's range (each)
lineItems.description: Max when each page lists neighbourhoods, any trip charge and recent hauls in that town.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep with haul photos
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A real before-and-after of a garage or basement junk haul on your Google profile every week, so the listing looks as busy as the truck."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each haul
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The evening after each junk pickup, a short thank-you asks for a review and mentions what got donated. Those reviews do the selling."

whatElseYouSell.name: Realtor and property manager outreach
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short monthly note to the agents and landlords in your area, pointing at the cleanout page and a same-week junk removal slot."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the estate cleanout page is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Truck wrap artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The hauling truck is parked on a different street every hour. A wrap with the booking address and 'priced by the load' turns it into the best ad you own."
whatElseYouSell.when: Right after launch, coordinated with their wrap shop.

whatElseYouSell.name: Spring cleanout campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One campaign in March for garage and shed junk, pointing at open pickup windows and the photo quote."

whatElseYouSell.name: Estate cleanout brochure for attorneys and realtors
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A calm, printed estate cleanout sheet that probate attorneys and listing agents can hand to families, with your process and booking address."

whatElseYouSell.name: Short haul videos for social media
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A day filming a full garage turning empty, cut into short clips. Satisfying junk removal videos get shared by people who'll need you later."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, at a job where the owner agrees in writing.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The estate sale company that calls you to haul what didn't sell needs a site with upcoming sales and photos. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: They run on repeat sales and need an online presence; the hauler finishing their jobs is a trusted voice.

withoutAI.route: Listing agents who need houses emptied
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Listing agents phone you to empty a garage of junk before the photographer comes. Their sellers deserve a vetted-vendors page, with your hauling first."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents recommend vendors on every listing and pay for pages that make them look organised.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The senior move manager who books you for the leftover furniture after a downsizing has no site worth sending a family to. I fix that."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Move managers work with families in hard moments and pick vendors carefully; the hauler's word carries weight.

withoutAI.whoPays: The remodeler, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The handyman who calls you to haul old cabinets books by text. A simple site with a request form is quick for both of you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small contractors need sites and trust the hauler who clears their jobs.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The storage facility that calls you to clear out abandoned units has a rental page from years ago. Your cleanout work gets me a meeting."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Facilities have steady budgets and rely on the junk hauler for unit cleanouts.

withoutAI.route: Thrift stores that take your donations
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The thrift store where you drop donated furniture has no pickup request page. I can build one, and your hauls go in the story."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Thrift stores want more donations and already know the hauler as a reliable source.

withAI.route: Inventory list builder for estate sale companies
withAI.pitchLine: "Walk the house with a phone, talk through each room, and get a draft item list for the estate sale with the leftovers flagged for the junk haul."
withAI.whyItWorks: Inventory takes them days. The hauler gets a clean list of what's coming.

withAI.pitchLine: "Sellers answer a few questions and get a prep plan with the junk haul, the cleaning and the photo date in the right order."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents want listings ready on time, and the hauler is the first vendor in the plan.

withAI.route: Downsizing planner for senior move managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Families list the furniture and the new apartment size, and the planner suggests what fits, what's donated and what the hauler takes."
withAI.whyItWorks: Move managers repeat this sorting with every family; the hauler gets the leftover load.

withAI.route: Auction listing writer for storage facilities
withAI.pitchLine: "The facility photographs a unit going to auction and gets a draft listing, with a junk haul booked for whatever doesn't sell."
withAI.whyItWorks: Storage operators write these listings by hand; the hauler is already the cleanout vendor.

withAI.route: Donation pickup triage for thrift stores
withAI.pitchLine: "Donors send a photo of the furniture, and the store's assistant says yes, no or 'call the junk hauler', from the store's own rules."
withAI.whyItWorks: Stores turn down items daily and want a kind way to say no that still helps the donor.

withAI.pitchLine: "The remodeler describes the demo, and the helper estimates the debris loads and books the hauling on the right day."
withAI.whyItWorks: Built for a contractor the junk client already hauls for, so the introduction is easy.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back with load prices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "You're carrying a dresser down the stairs and miss a call. The caller gets a text with junk prices by the load and a photo quote link within a minute."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the business number forwarded and wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: On-the-way text with arrival window
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the hauling crew leaves the last job, the next customer gets a text that the truck is twenty minutes out, so nobody waits in the driveway."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the booking calendar and a one-tap button for the driver.

softwareAI.name: Photo quote from customer pictures
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers send pictures of the junk pile, and you get a draft load size and price from your own price guide to approve and send back."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the load-size guide and a set of past jobs with photos and final prices. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for hauls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Somebody praises how fast the hot tub disappeared; a reply thanking them and mentioning the haul is ready for you at the dump."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Day planner by truck and dump run
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Junk jobs ordered by street with dump, donation and recycling stops slotted in, so the truck is never full on the wrong side of town."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs addresses, the drop-off sites they use and truck capacity.

softwareAI.name: Load and disposal log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each load's weight, dump fee and donation drop logged from the phone, so the owner knows which junk jobs actually made money."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their dump tickets and drop-off routine.

softwareAI.name: Booking chat for 'do you take this' questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do you take paint' and 'how much for a piano' from your own junk list and prices, then books a pickup window."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the take-and-can't list, prices and calendar. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Donation receipt sender
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When donated furniture from a junk haul is dropped off, the customer gets the receipt and a thank-you without the owner typing anything."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the donation partners' receipt process.

softwareAI.name: Estate cleanout project tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Room by room, what the family keeps, what's donated and what's hauled, with photos the out-of-town family can check from home."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once estate cleanouts come through the site. Needs their cleanout process.

softwareAI.name: After-hours receptionist for same-day hauls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Someone calls at 8pm needing a couch gone before the new one arrives, and the receptionist takes the details and books tomorrow's first junk slot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the calendar, prices and take list. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Contractor debris account page
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Remodelers request a debris haul for a job address, see their past pickups and get one invoice a month."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their contractor customers and billing terms.

softwareAI.name: Helper applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "People applying to haul junk with you answer questions about lifting, licences and early starts, and you only call the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any month they're hiring. Needs must-haves, pay and schedule. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Resale item tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Good furniture pulled from junk hauls, with photos, asking price and where it's stored, so resale money isn't forgotten in the shed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, if they resell items. Needs their storage spot and resale habits.

softwareAI.name: Customer message sorter for junk jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Photo quotes, reschedules and 'can you also take the shed' messages get sorted and drafted, so the owner answers between hauls."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the business text line or inbox. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per junk load
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See what each quarter, half and full load really earned after dump fees, fuel and labour, so the price guide is set from real numbers."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a few months of the disposal log and crew hours.

softwareAI.name: Estate cleanout walkthrough notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through an estate walkthrough room by room, and get a draft cleanout scope, load count and quote to send the family."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after the estate tracker. Needs past estate quotes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Realtor portal for listing cleanouts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Agents book a junk cleanout for a listing, add the lockbox note and get before-and-after pictures for the seller in one place."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once a few agents use them regularly. Needs agent contacts and access rules.

softwareAI.name: Repeat-customer check-in
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Six months after a garage junk haul, the customer gets a friendly note asking if the garage needs another clear-out before winter."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs past jobs with dates and job type.

softwareAI.name: Quote follow-up writer for unbooked hauls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A photo quote that didn't turn into a booking gets a polite follow-up in your voice two days later, with this week's open hauling windows."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the photo quote. Needs quote outcomes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Truck and trailer maintenance log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Oil changes, tyre checks and dump-trailer repairs for each hauling truck, with reminders, so a breakdown doesn't cancel a full day of junk jobs."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the truck list and their service history, even from receipts.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the photo quote for independent junk haulers
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Junk removal companies, monthly per account
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a photo-to-price tool for one junk hauler. Every independent truck answers 'how much for this pile' twenty times a day."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for it and taught you the load sizes. Independents everywhere fight franchise ads with the same problem.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: License load pricing and booking to a truck and trailer dealer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Everyone who buys a dump trailer from you to start hauling junk needs a booking site on day one. Bundle mine."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Dealers sell to new hauling businesses and want them to succeed and come back for a second truck.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give every member junk hauler a template with load pricing, the take list and estate cleanout pages as a membership perk."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Owner groups need reasons to join and renew, and one agreement reaches many trucks.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your clients' families need a house emptied before it sells. One vendor page with a vetted cleanout and hauling crew they can book."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Attorneys refer vendors constantly and value pages that make the estate process easier for grieving families.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label junk removal template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency builds hauling sites from scratch. License my template with load pictures, the photo quote and estate pages done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the client; you sell them the part you've already perfected.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every abandoned unit across your facilities gets a junk cleanout booked from one page, with photos for your records."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Operators clear units constantly and pay to stop calling around for haulers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Furniture left behind at move-out gets a junk pickup booked from one board, across every property you run."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Operators turn units every month and want one vendor flow instead of phone calls.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same junk removal stack in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New hauling clients in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "One junk hauler per area is my rule. {City} has its truck; the suburbs past the ring road don't yet."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the load guide, the photo quote and the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Charity thrift chains' donation pickup network
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Donors who can't haul furniture themselves get matched to vetted local junk haulers who drop it at your nearest store."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chains want more donations without running trucks, and haulers want the goodwill.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your students are starting junk removal businesses with one truck. Bundle my site template into the course."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Coaches sell to new owners who all need the same site, and they bring the buyers to you.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Senior living communities' downsizing partners page
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New residents need a house cleared before move-in. One partners page with vetted cleanout and hauling crews they can book."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Communities want move-ins to go smoothly, and a trusted hauler removes a reason families delay.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A booking site or photo quote for your junk business that someone never finished? Send me the login and I'll tell you what's salvageable."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded owners already decided to buy; they want someone who has finished one.

upsellLadder.offer: Junk removal booking site plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The junk removal site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new load price is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: A month live, and the first online booking has come through.
upsellLadder.line: "Your first online junk booking read your reviews before booking. Let's add one after every haul."

upsellLadder.trigger: Customers keep texting photos of junk piles and asking for a price.
upsellLadder.line: "People already send you pictures. Let the photo quote draft the load size before you even look."

upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of bookings show agents or landlords booking more than once.
upsellLadder.line: "Those repeat agents are the best junk customers you have. Let's find the ones who don't know you yet."

upsellLadder.trigger: They book their first estate cleanout through the site.
upsellLadder.line: "Estate cleanouts are your biggest hauling tickets. Give the family a room-by-room view and they'll recommend you."

upsellLadder.trigger: The missed-call log shows evening calls going unanswered.
upsellLadder.line: "Those evening calls want junk gone tomorrow. The receptionist books them while you're off the truck."

upsellLadder.offer: Day planner by truck and dump run
upsellLadder.trigger: They add a second truck or a helper crew.
upsellLadder.line: "Two trucks means two routes and twice the dump runs. Plan the hauling day before it starts."
